newsitem.title: USA: US attache sees gain in Argentina oilseed crushing.
newsitem.headline: US attache sees gain in Argentina oilseed crushing.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache said Argentina's role as a world leader in vegetable oil and meal exports will become "more pronounced" due to continuing rapid investment in its oilseed crushing physical plant.

In a report dated March 3 that was released in Washington Friday, the attache said industry consultants estimate that Argentina will soon have 24.5 million tonnes of crushing capacity when currently active construction projects are finished, about three million tonnes more than the current level.
The attache said current investment plans, if realized, could result in about 29 million tonnes of total crushing capacity within two years.

"Additionally, this growth in capacity is expected to positively influence domestic oilseed production and further increase the competitiveness of the Argentine meal and oil export sector in world markets," the attache wrote.

The attache said the increased investment would also likely decrease the quantity of seeds exported from the region as Argentine crushers, in an attempt to run plants closer to full capacity than the current 75 percent, could end up drawing more seed from neighboring countries into Argentina as well as adding value to their own production.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
